response.description: Managed connectors in Azure Functions are now generally available, enabling developers to build event-driven applications that react to events and take actions across Microsoft 365, SaaS, and business systems using the familiar Azure Functions programming model. Managed connectors, provided through the Azure Connector Namespace, wrap service-specific APIs and handle authentication, webhooks, retries, and more, so developers can focus on their application logic while Azure manages the underlying connections and integration infrastructure.Developers can build with C#, Python, and Node.js and use connector triggers together with strongly typed Connector SDK clients for a wide range of services including Outlook, SharePoint, and Dataverse, as well as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and many other third-party systems. Built through close collaboration between Azure Connector Namespace and Azure Functions, managed connectors are integrated directly into the Functions programming and runtime experience. Functions support both webhook and polling trigger models with automatic scaling, giving developers flexibility in how applications receive and process events.Managed connectors work alongside existing Azure Functions triggers and bindings, so developers can add integrations incrementally to new or existing applications. This makes it possible to combine business-system events with custom code, Azure services, and AI capabilities while continuing to use the deployment, scaling, and monitoring experience developers already use with Azure Functions.Learn more.
response.title: Generally Available: Managed Connectors in Azure Functions
